subject: General Knowledge
description: Indian painting styles + traditional martial arts — exam-favourite niches

questions.explanation: Madhubani (Mithila) painting — from Mithila region of Bihar (and parts of Nepal). Geometric patterns, no blank space. Typically painted on floors / walls, now on paper/cloth. Themes: Hindu deities, nature, weddings. GI-tagged.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the PAINTING STYLE with its STATE. A. Warli.  B. Kalamkari.  C. Tanjore.  D. Phad. List-II: 1. Maharashtra (tribal).  2. Andhra Pradesh / Telangana.  3. Tamil Nadu (gold foil).  4. Rajasthan (scroll).
questions.explanation: Warli — Adivasi tribal geometric art, Maharashtra (Thane / Palghar). Kalamkari — 'kalam' (pen) + 'kari' (work), hand/block painted, AP/Telangana. Tanjore — 3D effect with gold foil, gems, TN. Phad — scroll paintings, Rajasthan, narrating religious epics.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: PATTACHITRA painting is a traditional art of:
questions.explanation: Pattachitra — cloth-based scroll painting (Patta = cloth, Chitra = picture). Depicts Jagannath / Vaishnava themes. Raghurajpur village (near Puri, Odisha) is a heritage craft village. GI-tagged. Puri-Raghurajpur region.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Match the MARTIAL ART with the STATE. A. Kalaripayattu.  B. Silambam.  C. Gatka.  D. Thang-ta. List-II: 1. Kerala.  2. Tamil Nadu.  3. Punjab.  4. Manipur.
questions.explanation: Kalaripayattu — Kerala — considered one of the oldest martial arts in the world. Silambam — TN — staff-fighting. Gatka — Punjab/Sikh — originally a training system; stick/sword combat. Thang-ta — Manipur — sword + spear. Others: Mallakhamba (pole gymnastics, MP/Maharashtra), Cheraw (Mizoram bamboo dance).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The MUGHAL school of painting reached its peak under:
questions.explanation: Jahangir (r. 1605-1627) — zenith of Mughal miniature painting. Known for naturalistic animal and bird studies. Noted artists: Ustad Mansur (naturalist), Abul Hasan, Bishandas. Akbar laid the foundations (Tutinama, Hamzanama). Aurangzeb discouraged figurative art.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: KALAMEZHUTHU / KALAM is a ritual floor painting tradition of:
questions.explanation: Kalamezhuthu — ritual floor drawing in Kerala temples, using coloured powders. Depicts deities, erased after ritual. Rangoli / Muggu (AP) / Alpana (Bengal) / Kolam (TN) / Mandana (Rajasthan) are related floor-art traditions across India.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Raja Ravi Varma (1848-1906) — the 'Indian Michelangelo' — is famous for oil-painting style depictions of:

options.option_text: Scenes from Hindu mythology (Ramayana, Mahabharata) and regal portraits

questions.explanation: Raja Ravi Varma — Keralite painter who fused European techniques (oil, realism) with Indian mythological themes. Famous works: 'Galaxy of Musicians', 'Shakuntala', 'Damayanti', portraits of Travancore royalty. Pioneered mass-printed lithographs of Hindu deities.
